units.name: Hunt-Sovereign

unitRules.name: Herald of the War-moon
unitRules.text: Somewhere above the battle, one of the Rangdan war-moons is listening for this voice. The War-moon Strike may be fired in place of the Hunt-Sovereign's other Weapons in a Shooting Attack, even if the Hunt-Sovereign is Locked in Combat or is not in line of sight of the target, and its Blast Marker scatters as normal for a Barrage weapon.

options.text: May exchange its Sovereign's Glaive for the Fang of the First Xenocide for +20 points.
May have one item from the Relics of the Hunt selected for it.

units.note: A hunt-lord of the Rangda, one of the tall vulpine masters the Imperium spent three Xenocides trying to erase. Written for this list.

units.name: Rangda Huntmaster

options.text: May exchange its Spine Glaive for an item from the Rangdan Hunting Weapons list, or for a Severing Maul for +20 points.
May exchange its Shadow Pistol for an item from the Rangdan Sidearms list.
May exchange its Spine Glaive for the Fang of the First Xenocide for +25 points.
May have one item from the Relics of the Hunt selected for it.

units.note: The officer who leads a hunt-pack in the field. Written for this list.

units.name: Collar-Wright

unitRules.name: Master of Collars
unitRules.text: The Collar-Wright fits the collars and knows every one by its signal. A Model with this Special Rule may use the Collar-master Special Rule twice in each Player Turn, selecting a different Unit each time, and may select a Unit with any Model within 18" of it. In addition, Units with the Neural Collars Special Rule that have any Model within 18" of a Collar-Wright count as being within 12" of a friendly Rangdan Model.

options.text: May exchange its Spine Glaive for an item from the Rangdan Hunting Weapons list, or for a Severing Maul for +20 points.
May exchange its Shadow Pistol for an item from the Rangdan Sidearms list.
May exchange its Spine Glaive for the Fang of the First Xenocide for +25 points.
May have one item from the Relics of the Hunt selected for it.

units.note: The Rangda who keeps the herd. Written for this list.

units.name: Hunt-Pack

options.text: One Rangda Hunter may be upgraded to a Pack-Alpha for +15 points.
Any Model may exchange its Spine Glaive for an item from the Rangdan Hunting Weapons list.
For every three Models in the Unit, one may exchange its Spine Glaive for a Severing Maul for +20 points.
Any Model may exchange its Shadow Pistol for an item from the Rangdan Sidearms list.

units.note: The Rangda as the Dark Angels remembered them: towering, quick and hard to put down. Written for this list.

units.name: Shadow Lancers

options.text: One Shadow Lancer may be upgraded to a Lance-Alpha for +15 points.
Any Model may exchange its Shadow Lance for a Shadow Caster.

units.note: Rangda carrying the heavy shadow weapons that unmake tanks. The Shadow Caster trades the lance for a burst that pins infantry. Written for this list.

units.name: Mimics

unitRules.name: Stolen Voices
unitRules.text: The Mimics speak with the voices of the dead: a sergeant calling the retreat, a brother screaming for help from the wrong direction. Shooting Attacks made by a Unit that only includes Models with this Special Rule gain the Panic (1) Special Rule.

options.text: One Mimic may be upgraded to a Mimic-Alpha for +15 points.

units.note: Canon credits the Rangda with mimicry and never says what it was. These are the hunters who use it. Written for this list.

units.name: Tendril Skiffs

options.text: Any Tendril Skiff may exchange its Shadow Blaster for a Shadow Lance for +10 points.

units.note: A small iron jellyfish, all spines and trailing metal tendrils, the same shape as the Rangdan warships. Written for this list.

units.name: Iron Medusa

options.text: May exchange its Turret Mounted Shadow Cannon for a Turret Mounted Shadow Lance Array for +25 points.
May exchange its 2 Hull Mounted Tendril Flails for 2 Hull Mounted Shadow Blasters for +5 points.

units.note: The Rangdan battle tank: a floating iron bell trailing a curtain of flails. Written for this list.

units.name: Spine-Leviathan

options.text: May exchange its 2 Sponson Mounted Shadow Cannons for 2 Sponson Mounted Shadow Lance Arrays for +15 points.

units.note: A war-moon's lander, as big as a Fellblade. Written for this list.

units.name: Tendril Barge

options.text: May exchange its 2 Hull Mounted Tendril Flails for 2 Hull Mounted Shadow Blasters for +5 points.

units.note: A hunting barge with room for four Rangda, who drop from its tendrils straight into a charge. Written for this list.

units.name: Shadow Kite
units.note: A flat ray of black iron trailing two spines; the Rangdan answer to an interceptor. Written for this list.

units.name: War-moon Regent

unitRules.name: Voice of the War-moon
unitRules.text: A Regent rules a war-moon, and the moon answers every time it speaks. The War-moon Barrage may be fired in place of the Regent's other Weapons in every Shooting Attack it makes, even if the Regent is Locked in Combat or is not in line of sight of the target, and its Blast Marker scatters as normal for a Barrage weapon.

units.note: The master of a war-moon, come down to see a world taken in person. A Primarch-level threat. Written for this list.

units.name: Ithrakk, the First Voice

unitRules.name: Herald of the War-moon
unitRules.text: Somewhere above the battle, one of the Rangdan war-moons is listening for this voice. The War-moon Strike may be fired in place of the Hunt-Sovereign's other Weapons in a Shooting Attack, even if the Hunt-Sovereign is Locked in Combat or is not in line of sight of the target, and its Blast Marker scatters as normal for a Barrage weapon.

unitRules.name: The First Voice
unitRules.text: Ithrakk came through at Advex-Mors before anyone knew what the Rangda were, and spoke to the garrison in their commander's voice for a week. Ithrakk's Hunting Cry has a range of 18" and the Pinning (3) Special Rule instead of Pinning (2).

units.note: The first Rangda the Imperium met, at Advex-Mors. Silent Choir. Written for this list.

units.name: Hunt-Court

unitRules.name: Sworn to the Hunt
unitRules.text: While a friendly Hunt-Sovereign, War-moon Regent or Ithrakk has joined a Unit with this Special Rule, all Models in the Unit gain a modifier of +1 to their Attacks Characteristic.

units.note: The hunters who walk beside a Sovereign, shroud-fields and all. Written for this list.

units.name: Brood-ship

options.text: May exchange its Turret Mounted Shadow Cannon for a Turret Mounted Shadow Lance Array for +25 points.

units.note: The big iron jellyfish that carries a hunt, or a herd, down from orbit. Written for this list.

units.name: Medusa Drop-ship
units.note: A flying jellyfish with a hunt inside it: five Rangda dropped wherever the war-moon points. Written for this list.

units.name: Spine-pod
units.note: A spined seed fired down from a war-moon with four Rangda or a Spine-Stalker inside. Written for this list.

units.name: Collar-Ark

unitRules.name: Collar Beacon
unitRules.text: The Ark carries the herd and broadcasts the collar signal over it. Units with the Neural Collars Special Rule that have any Model within 12" of a Model with this Special Rule, or are Embarked on it, count as being within 12" of a friendly Rangdan Model.

units.note: A Rangdan herding vessel: it carries a Thrall squad and keeps every collar around it obedient. Written for this list.

units.name: Skyhunters

options.text: One Skyhunter may be upgraded to a Sky-Alpha for +15 points.
Any Model may exchange its Spine Glaive for an item from the Rangdan Hunting Weapons list.
For every three Models in the Unit, one may exchange its Spine Glaive for a Severing Maul for +20 points.
Any Model may exchange its Shadow Pistol for an item from the Rangdan Sidearms list.

units.note: Rangda on grav-harnesses who drop out of the sky onto whatever the Cry has pinned. Written for this list.

units.name: Ironhide Hunters

options.text: One Ironhide Hunter may be upgraded to an Ironhide-Alpha for +15 points.
For every three Models in the Unit, one may exchange its Great Glaive for a Severing Maul for +15 points.

units.note: Rangda in grown war-plate, the hunt's answer to Terminators. Written for this list.

units.name: Hunt-Hounds

unitRules.name: Beasts of the Hunt
unitRules.text: Long-legged hunting beasts from the Rangda's own worlds, loosed ahead of the hunt. Models with this Special Rule do not count as Rangdan Models for the Neural Collars, Collar-master or Living Shields Special Rules, and are not affected by the Long Hunt or Silent Choir Tacticas.

units.note: The Rangda's hunting beasts. Heedless, like Fenrisian wolves: they run prey down, they don't hold ground. Written for this list.

units.name: Shroud-Weaver

options.text: May exchange its Spine Glaive for an item from the Rangdan Hunting Weapons list, or for a Severing Maul for +20 points.
May exchange its Shadow Pistol for an item from the Rangdan Sidearms list.
May exchange its Spine Glaive for the Fang of the First Xenocide for +25 points.
May have one item from the Relics of the Hunt selected for it.

units.note: The Rangda who tends the shroud-fields, and spreads one over the pack it walks with. Written for this list.

units.name: Moon-callers
units.note: Rangda carrying a piece of a war-moon's targeting array, calling small strikes down from orbit. Burning Sky moon-callers reach 78". Written for this list.

units.name: Spine-Stalker

options.text: May exchange its Shadow Lance for a Shadow Cannon.

units.note: A tall iron walker on spined legs, trailing tendrils, ridden by a Rangda hunt-lord too old to run. Written for this list.

units.name: Thrall Cohort

options.text: For every 10 Models in the Unit, one may exchange its Lasrifle for an item from the Captured Heavy Weapons list.

units.note: Imperial Army troops taken on a Rangdan-tainted world, still in their old uniforms. Uses Imperial Army models.

units.name: Collared Auxilia

options.text: For every 10 Models in the Unit, one may exchange its Lasrifle for an item from the Captured Special Weapons list.

units.note: Captured Solar Auxilia in their void armour. Uses Solar Auxilia models.

units.name: Collared Ogryns
units.note: Captured abhumans, the herd's favourite thing to overload. Uses Ogryn models.

units.name: Thrall Armour

options.text: May exchange its Turret Mounted Battlecannon for one of the following:
May exchange its Hull (Front) Mounted Heavy bolter for one of the following:
May take one of the following pairs of sponson weapons:
May take any of the following:

units.note: A captured Leman Russ with a collared crew. Neural Collars still applies: with no Rangda within 12" its crew may not declare Reactions.

units.name: Thrall Carrier

options.text: May exchange its Pintle Mounted Heavy stubber for one of the following:

units.note: A captured Aurox with a collared driver. Uses Solar Auxilia models.

units.name: Thrall Dracosan
units.note: A captured Dracosan big enough for a whole Thrall Cohort. Uses Solar Auxilia models.

units.name: Thrall Malcador

options.text: May exchange its Two Sponson Mounted Multi-lasers for Two Sponson Mounted Lascannons for +15 points.

units.note: A captured Malcador with a collared crew. Uses Imperial Army models.

units.name: The Broken

unitRules.name: Still in There
unitRules.text: They know their brothers' names, and sometimes they say them. Enemy Models with the Infantry Type that are Locked in Combat with a Unit with this Special Rule gain the Hatred (Thrall) Special Rule in that Combat.

units.note: Collared Legionaries: the reason the Xenocide records are sealed. Uses Legion models in their own colours. Written for this list.

units.name: Marshal Casimir Vehl

unitRules.name: The Marshal's Collar
unitRules.text: Vehl's collar is wired to every collar under his old command. Units with the Neural Collars Special Rule that have any Model within 12" of Casimir Vehl count as being within 12" of a friendly Rangdan Model. Vehl himself does not.

unitRules.name: Orders in His Old Voice
unitRules.text: Once per battle, at the start of its Controlling Player's Shooting Phase, Vehl may select up to two friendly Units with the Thrall Trait that have any Model within 12" of him. Until the end of that Phase, Shooting Attacks made by those Units gain the Pinning (1) Special Rule.

units.note: An Imperial Army marshal taken with his whole regiment, who still gives orders in his own voice. Iron Chain. Written for this list.

units.name: Thrall Gun-teams

options.text: Any Thrall Gun-team may exchange its Heavy bolter for an item from the Gun-team Weapons list.

units.note: Captured heavy weapon crews, two collared gunners to a model. Uses Imperial Army models.

units.name: Thrall Basilisk
units.note: A captured Basilisk with a collared crew. Uses Solar Auxilia models.

units.name: Thrall Knight

options.text: May exchange its Rapid-fire battle cannon for a Thermal cannon for +15 points.

units.note: A Questoris Knight whose pilot was collared inside the Throne Mechanicum. Neural Collars applies to its Reactions. Uses Questoris models.

units.name: Slaugth Dream-Eater

unitRules.name: Dream Eater
unitRules.text: The Slaugth eat brains for the memories in them. When a Model with this Special Rule Removes an enemy Model with the Command Sub-Type as a Casualty in a Challenge, it regains all of its lost Wounds.

options.text: May exchange its Necrotic Projector for a Necrotic Spewer for +10 points.
May take a Corpse-cloak for +10 points.

units.note: Canon places the Slaugth at Rangda during the Xenocides and says nothing more about why. Here they follow the hunts and eat the dead. Taking a Dream-Eater in a Command slot unlocks the Carrion Court. Written for this list.

units.name: Slaugth Kindred

options.text: For every three Models in the Unit, one may exchange its Necrotic Projector for a Necrotic Spewer for +10 points.
For every three Models in the Unit, one may exchange its Worm-grasp for a Nerve-lash for +5 points.

units.note: Three-metre shapes of writhing worms in robes. Written for this list.

units.name: Vassal Swarm
units.note: Floating flesh constructs the Slaugth grow and send ahead of them. Written for this list.

units.name: Harvester

options.text: May exchange its 2 Necrotic Projectors for 2 Necrotic Spewers for +15 points.

units.note: A vehicle-sized mass of flesh and metal that gathers the dead. Written for this list.

units.name: Slaugth Ambush-craft

unitRules.name: Living Hull
unitRules.text: The craft is grown, not built, and it closes its own wounds. At the start of its Controlling Player's turn, roll a Dice for a Model with this Special Rule that has lost any Hull Points: on a 5+ it regains one lost Hull Point.

units.note: The Slaugth void-craft that struck from ambush at Rangda: a ribbed flesh hull that comes in low from the board edge. Written for this list.

units.name: Charnel Barge

unitRules.name: Living Hull
unitRules.text: The barge is grown, not built, and it closes its own wounds. At the start of its Controlling Player's turn, roll a Dice for a Model with this Special Rule that has lost any Hull Points: on a 5+ it regains one lost Hull Point.

units.note: A floating hull of flesh over a metal frame that carries the Kindred to the dead, and opens to let them feed. Written for this list.

units.name: The Hollow Choir

unitRules.name: Feast of Minds
unitRules.text: When a Model with this Special Rule Removes an enemy Model with the Command Sub-Type as a Casualty, in a Challenge or not, it regains all of its lost Wounds.

unitRules.name: Stolen Memories
unitRules.text: The Choir has eaten the minds of Dark Angels, and remembers how Legions fight. Once per battle, at the start of the opposing Player's turn, its Controlling Player may name one Advanced Reaction. That Reaction may not be declared until the end of the battle turn.

units.note: A Slaugth elder that speaks in a chorus of Dark Angel voices. Unlocks the Carrion Court like a Dream-Eater. Written for this list.
